top_choice_rationale: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a mature, independently confirmed general method that solved distinct mechanistic problems (amine binding, beta-hydride elimination from amido complexes, difficult C-N reductive elimination) through ligand design and is now a default disconnection in medicinal, process and materials chemistry. The two-name allocation (Buchwald, Hartwig) is clean and the citation can stand apart from the 2010 prize and from Kosugi's tin-amide precursor. Base editing is the stronger new-capability story but carries the Kondo/Nishida attribution problem and proximity to the 2020 prize; degraders are scientifically real but the PROTAC and cereblon strands and the third seat remain contested and no degrader is yet approved.
